title: chock run
description: What one `chock run` found. Printed by `chock run --json`, and cached at `.chock/last-run.json` — where it holds the last result for each gate rather than one run, so that running one gate does not erase what another found. `chock explain` reads it back without paying for the gates again.

chock.description: The chock that produced this run.

gates.description: Every gate the run touched, in the order it ran them.

verdict.description: `passed` met the bar, `tripped` did not, `cannot_run` produced no measurement at all. A cannot_run is never a pass: treating it as one is the mistake that makes the whole thing worthless.

exit_code.description: What this gate alone would exit with: 0 passed, 1 tripped, 2 could not run. A run exits with the worst of them.

measured.description: What this run measured, summed over the gate's keys. Absent for a pass/fail gate, which produces a verdict rather than a number.

baseline.description: What the committed baseline holds for the same keys. Absent for a pass/fail gate.

cannot_run_reason.description: Why no measurement was produced. Present exactly when the verdict is cannot_run.

findings.description: Findings and scope advisories. A passing gate may include advisory entries; these do not change its verdict or measured count.

rerun.description: The narrowest command that re-runs this one gate. Fix, then run this rather than the whole set.

ran_at.description: When this gate ran, in seconds since the Unix epoch. Written only into the cached record at .chock/last-run.json, which holds the last result for each gate rather than one run: without it a reader cannot tell a result this run produced from one an earlier run left, and would read a stale pass as a current one.

fix.description: What to do about a gate that tripped, or about one that could not run because its tool is missing or is another build of it, in one sentence for a person or an agent. Absent for a gate that passed, and where chock has no advice.

recalled.description: True where this verdict was answered from an earlier run's record rather than taken again, every input the gate names having hashed the same: the files chock's walk can see, the config, the baseline, the versions of the tools it shells out to, and chock's own version. Absent means the gate ran. A gate that names no inputs is never recalled, and a `cannot_run` is never kept, because nothing was measured and the tool that was missing may be installed by the time anybody asks again.

file.description: Relative to the project root, so it means the same on the next machine. Empty when the finding is about the gate rather than a file, in which case `item` names the subject.

item.description: The function, lint or measure this is about, where the file alone is not the subject.

message.description: What is wrong, in one line.

places.description: The other places the finding is about, each named by what it is to this one: the copy of a body, the statement that costs most, the part that could move.

fix.description: The change that clears this finding, in one sentence, where the gate can name one.

grade.description: `candidate` where the gate cannot settle the finding from the source: a lead to judge, which never trips the gate. Absent for a finding, which counts.

role.description: What this place is to the finding, such as `copy`, `costs most` or `can move out`.

last.description: The last line, where the place spans more than one.

item.description: The function, type or statement at this place.
